name: GiveDirectly cash transfers, wellbeing analysis
summary: Sends cash transfers of about $1,000 to poor households in East Africa. The Happier Lives Institute's estimate of GiveDirectly's effect on wellbeing, from its meta-analysis of cash transfers' effects on life satisfaction and mental health, including spillovers to the household.

source.title: Cash transfers cost-effectiveness analysis
source.license: © Happier Lives Institute; no licence published

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000
rows.explainer: HLI's current figure for GiveDirectly, which it uses as the benchmark for its other charities. HLI's earlier, more detailed model (2022) put it at 8.2 WELLBYs per $1,000. HLI's report explains the meta-analysis behind it; the summary sheet publishes only the result, so this model has a single input.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: About 16% of GiveDirectly's costs are not transfers; we guess half of that is staff pay, as in our GiveDirectly model.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Our judgment, as in our GiveDirectly model.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: WELLBYs per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
